query: A TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy has been reported in a single-phase BCC, dendritic state, with a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain under lower-temperature testing, but at 1273 K it retains only 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain. For its use as an intermediate layer that transfers heat between W and CuCrZr while preserving structural integrity, what single intervention could overcome this loss of strength at elevated temperature? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the reported baseline, define the applicable thermal and mechanical boundary conditions, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Engineering the microstructure of the TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy with optimized grain size and distribution through a controlled thermo-mechanical processing intervention will enhance its yield strength and compressive strength at elevated temperatures.
generation.intervention: Thermo-mechanical processing with controlled grain refinement and distribution
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and solid solution strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength increased to 500 MPa and compressive strength to 600 MPa at 30% strain
generation.baseline: Reported yield strength of 330 MPa and compressive strength of 423 MPa at 30% strain
generation.boundary: Thermal boundary: 1273 K, Mechanical boundary: 30% strain
generation.uncertainty: The actual outcome may vary depending on the specific thermo-mechanical processing parameters and the resulting microstructure

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled thermo-mechanical processing of TiVNbTa alloy with varying grain refinement and distribution, followed by mechanical testing at 1273 K
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and compressive strength at 30% strain are not increased by at least 20% relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
